newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Micro profits lower than expected.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Micro profits lower than expected.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. on Tuesday reported weaker-than-expected second-quarter profits, reflecting the rapid shift toward newer-generation semiconductors and pricing pressure on older models.

For the three months ended June 29, Advanced Micro earned $9.97 million, or 7 cents per fully diluted share, on sales of $594.56 million. The results compared with a loss of $34.67 million, or 26 cents a share, on sales of $455.08 milion a year ago.
The second-quarter results were below the consensus estimate of 22 cents a share in profits as compiled by First Call, which monitors Wall Street earnings forecasts.
In after-hours trading, Advanced Micro's stock tumbled to $36.625. Before the results were released, Advanced Micro had risen $1.125 to $39.125.

A spokesman for the chipmaker attributed the shortfall to the rapid shift toward AMD's newer chip, the K6, pricing pressure in the flash memory business and a disappointing quarter from its programmable logic business unit, Vantis.

He said the shift toward chips with so-called MMX technology, which improves the video and graphics on computers, was expected as computer makers phase out older models. The company said it is quickly converting production to the K6 chip.

"The marketplace is rapidly moving to MMX enhanced processors," said W.J. Sanders, chairman and chief executive officer. "The industry has acknowledged the excellence of the AMD-K6 MMX enhanced processor, and we are pleased with customer acceptance worldwide.

"We are executing well on our production ramp toward our goal of shipping millions of units in the second half of 1997," Sanders said. "Our overall book-to-bill ratio was greater than parity, resulting from strong bookings for the AMD-K6 MMX enhanced processor."
